result.summary: No ship: the revised counts reconcile, but the decision rule still understates the production losses, and the merge guidance understates the public commit’s reachability.

findings.title: [B] Squash-merge guidance understates reachability of the private descriptions
findings.body: The first commit contains descriptions learned from private sessions. Squashing keeps that commit out of main, but it remains reachable through the remote branch shown by `git branch -a --contains 97e45ff0`, as well as the PR ref. A SHA is not itself a ref, and the document gives no basis for saying GitHub will drop the object. The owner could mistake squash-merge for removal of the public exposure.
findings.recommendation: State that squashing only excludes the commit from main; it does not retract the published commit. Present branch and PR refs accurately, and treat any desired removal of the published material as a separate owner decision.

findings.title: [B] Decision rule still calls twelve live omissions an evaluation artefact
findings.body: Findings A and the disposition now say the twelve losses were made by the live 09-24 first pass and merely re-exposed by the empty ledger. The decision-rule item instead calls those losses repeat-pass behaviour and an artefact, then says only the four new-session losses are the live exposure. That can lead the owner to assess faithfulness using four production omissions when the record identifies sixteen.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish the artificial re-exposure from the twelve live first-pass omissions in the decision rule, then assess faithfulness against all sixteen production omissions.

next_steps: Correct the decision-rule wording and merge guidance before asking the owner to rule.
